title: Where the Interest Clock Starts on a Telephone Payment for an Auto Loans Borrower
content:
The date from which the interest clock runs, when a payment is taken on the telephone on a loan of the Auto Loans line, follows the balance owed on the borrower's Personal Credit Cards account measured against that card's credit limit.

**Where the balance owed is no more than 25 percent of the credit limit,** the clock runs from the date the installment then due falls on.

**Where the balance owed is more than 25 percent but no more than 50 percent of the credit limit,** the clock runs from the date the most recent charge was assessed on the loan.

**Where the balance owed is more than 50 percent of the credit limit,** the clock runs from the date of the last payment credited to the loan.

## The three bands side by side

| Balance owed as a share of the credit limit | Date the clock runs from |
|---|---|
| Up to and including 25 percent | The date the installment then due falls on |
| Above 25 percent and up to and including 50 percent | The date the most recent charge was assessed on the loan |
| Above 50 percent | The date of the last payment credited to the loan |

## The readings this rests on

Both readings come from the borrower's card account in the Personal Credit Cards line: the balance owed on it, and the credit limit recorded against it. Where the card shows a balance owed of 3000.00 USD against a credit limit of 12000.00 USD, the share is 25 percent, which is inside the first band because the band is read as up to and including its figure.

Where that same card shows a balance owed of 6000.00 USD against the same limit, the share is 50 percent, which is inside the second band for the same reason. A balance owed of 6000.01 USD against that limit falls into the third.

## How far apart the three dates can lie

The three dates can lie far apart on one loan. The band decides which of them the clock starts from, and nothing about the loan's own record moves the borrower between bands.
